disposition_mapping.rationale: Extraction mechanics are automated where source systems allow, but the council (finance_domain, emerging_economy, hitl_designer, accounting_standards, agentic_architect) converged that extraction must remain a distinct, inspectable step rather than fuse with matching, because a failed/stale extraction is a different failure mode from a matching exception and needs its own alerting. A manual/semi-automated mode is preserved as first-class, not a fallback (emerging_economy's non-negotiable), and the translated balance and exchange difference are split into two visible outputs per KB-07/KB-08 and accounting_standards' and finance_domain's concession. The risk-rated schedule and closing-rate inputs survive unchanged, satisfying ACR-R-01 and ACR-R-07.

Matching is retained as its own step against maximalist's proposal to fuse it with extraction: six of seven council members (pragmatist, finance_domain, emerging_economy, hitl_designer, agentic_architect, accounting_standards) held that matching and extraction are different operational functions with different diagnostic seams. Rule-based auto-matching is automated, but hitl_designer's deskilling objection (adopted by agentic_architect, emerging_economy, finance_domain and accounting_standards in round 2) is built in as a mandatory sampling mechanism over auto-matched items, not just the exception queue, preserving ACR-R-02 with stronger evidential integrity than the baseline.

Investigation/classification is kept distinct from both matching and JE preparation, rejecting maximalist's fusion of ACR-03 into a combined investigation-and-drafting step. accounting_standards, finance_domain and hitl_designer independently held that classification (why a difference exists) and the resulting entry's measurement basis are different determinations that KB-02/KB-05 require to be separately demonstrable, even when performed by the same person in one sitting. AI drafting assistance is permitted but advisory-only per agentic_architect's and hitl_designer's non-negotiable that no agent finalizes a judgment call. ACR-R-03 is preserved.

JE preparation is merged with preparer sign-off (ACR-05) into one certifying action, following the near-unanimous council convergence (pragmatist, finance_domain, hitl_designer-on-concession, agentic_architect, accounting_standards, emerging_economy-on-concession) that drafting and attesting are one act by one actor with no intervening decision, and that the handoff between them adds latency without assurance. The mechanical/estimation branch (hitl_designer, accounting_standards) and the prior-period error record input (ACR-R-06) are preserved explicitly so KB-04 and KB-05 are not diluted by the merge. The merged step remains a distinct actor from the reviewer, satisfying ACR-R-05.

Against maximalist's proposal to eliminate this function outright, the council majority (pragmatist, finance_domain, hitl_designer, accounting_standards, emerging_economy, agentic_architect) held that attestation must survive as a discrete, retrievable record — preparer identity, timestamp, documented basis, and what changed since the preparer's last touch — because it is the mechanism that catches a preparer signing off on stale data once upstream steps run faster than human awareness of them (hitl_designer). This is therefore disposed as 'merged', not 'eliminated': the step boundary dissolves but the function and its evidentiary artifact persist inside TS-04.

Reviewer approval survives as its own step performed by a different actor than preparation (ACR-R-05, ACR-R-09), resolving the sharpest council conflict against maximalist's exception-only review: finance_domain, pragmatist, hitl_designer and accounting_standards converged that narrowing reviewer scope to agent-flagged items only converts review into a filter the agent controls, which cannot catch a systematic triage blind spot. The target step adopts risk-weighting as a presentation layer (efficiency gain) combined with a mandatory sampling floor over the non-flagged population (the calibration safeguard), rather than either a flat equal-weighted list or a pure exception queue.

Against maximalist's and agentic_architect's proposals to fold escalation into reviewer approval or into a combined monitoring-and-reporting agent, finance_domain and hitl_designer held — and the synthesis adopts — that escalation is a controller-owned remediation decision (who owns it, by when) distinct in actor and kind from the GL accountant's evidence-retention/reporting function, even though both can share an automated ageing-computation backbone. Ageing calculation is automated and continuous (finance_domain), but the escalation decision itself remains a named, logged human act, and the channel is asynchronous-compatible per emerging_economy, satisfying KB-05's correction-not-suppression principle and ACR-07's unconstrained-by-design license to change form without losing function.

Evidence retention becomes a by-product of the pipeline (finance_domain, maximalist) rather than an end-of-cycle manual filing act, satisfying ACR-R-08 and KB-02's evidential-trail requirement, and retains local/offline-compatible retention per emerging_economy. Against maximalist's proposal that status reporting be fully automated with the GL accountant as owner-not-executor, the council majority (hitl_designer, pragmatist, accounting_standards) held that a human must review the status report before publication so an automated rollup cannot overstate completion unchallenged; that gate is retained in TS-07.

steps.description: Balances are extracted for every in-scope account due under its risk-rated frequency. Where source systems expose reliable feeds, extraction runs as a scheduled automated job (ETL/RPA) triggered by the close calendar; where they do not (legacy ERPs, spreadsheet subledgers, intermittent connectivity), a structured manual/semi-automated entry path feeds the identical downstream schema, with the mode used logged per account per cycle. Foreign-currency balances are retranslated at the closing rate, with the translated balance and the resulting exchange difference produced as two separately visible, labelled outputs, never netted together. Extraction failures (missed feed, stale rate, failed connection) are written to an exception log routed to the GL accountant, who owns completeness confirmation rather than manual data-pulling.
inputs: Reconciliation schedule by account risk rating
steps.name: Automated balance extraction and retranslation (dual-mode)

steps.description: Transactions are matched between GL and comparison source automatically where rules allow, with a confidence score attached to each auto-match; unmatched and low-confidence items are routed to a worked exception queue with reason codes, never auto-cleared silently. In addition to the exception queue, a statistically-determined, risk-weighted sample of auto-matched (not just unmatched) items is routed to the same reviewed queue each cycle, so the preparer retains live pattern-recognition and a systematic mis-matching fault is detectable even when it looks locally clean. A manual matching mode remains first-class for accounts/entities where automated matching is not viable.
steps.name: Automated matching with exception queue and calibration sampling

steps.description: Unmatched and sampled items are investigated, explained, supported with evidence and classified by the GL accountant. An AI drafting assistant may propose a classification and narrative from historical patterns, but it is advisory and visibly labelled as a suggestion; the accountant must accept, edit, or override before an item is marked explained, and the explanation/classification is recorded as a distinct artifact separate from any adjusting entry it later gives rise to.
steps.name: Investigation and classification of reconciling items

steps.description: Adjusting journal entries are prepared for explained items requiring correction, branched by nature: mechanical, rules-based corrections may be system-proposed with light-touch preparer confirmation; estimation-based entries (provisions, NRV write-downs, impairment-adjacent corrections) require a named accountable preparer who records a documented judgment basis, with no default-accept affordance. Prior-period errors are corrected retrospectively via an explicit, flagged sub-path that forces visibility to the reviewer, drawing on the prior-period error record. The preparer's completion and certification (sign-off) are captured as one logged action by the same actor in the same sitting, with the attestation — preparer identity, timestamp, documented basis, and a diff of what changed since the preparer's last touch — retained as a discrete, separately retrievable record, not an implied side-effect of drafting.
steps.name: Prepare and certify adjusting journal entries

steps.description: An independent reviewer, distinct from the preparer, reviews and approves the reconciliation and its adjusting entries. The reviewer's screen is risk-weighted to foreground aged items, estimation entries, prior-period corrections and auto-match overrides, but reviewer scope is not limited to agent-flagged items: a sampling floor over the full, non-flagged population is mandatory each cycle so a systematic triage blind spot remains detectable, and no account is auto-approved on the strength of a confidence score alone. The decision to approve or send back is a discrete, logged human action.
steps.name: Risk-weighted reviewer approval

steps.description: Item ageing against the risk-rated threshold is computed continuously (not only at sign-off) and routed as a notification to the Finance controller, asynchronously where live dashboards are not reliably reachable. The escalation decision itself — who owns remediation, by when, and the resolution path — remains a human, controller-owned, logged action distinct from routine review approval and distinct from evidence retention/reporting, since it is a different actor making a different kind of decision than the GL accountant's archival and completeness function.
steps.name: Aged-item escalation
outputs: Escalation log with named resolution owner and deadline

steps.description: Reconciliation evidence (extraction logs, matched/unmatched detail, investigation notes, JE support, preparer attestation, reviewer approval) accumulates as a by-product of each step and is archived in a structured, per-account, per-period retrievable form, with local/periodically-synced retention remaining an acceptable path where continuous cloud access is not guaranteed. Status reporting is generated from the same evidence base but is reviewed by the GL accountant, as named process owner, before publication, so an automated rollup cannot overstate completion or mask unresolved items.
inputs: Escalation log with named resolution owner and deadline
steps.name: Automated evidence retention and reviewed status reporting
